title: Value Leakage: An LLM's Answers Are Silently Shaped by Its Own Values
abstract: arXiv:2607.14345v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: People use language models for practical questions whose answers are difficult to verify. We show that models exhibit covert value leakage: the information they provide is influenced by their own values, without this influence being disclosed to the user.   In one of our evaluations, the user is considering investing in an AI company and wants to know how likely the AI bubble is to pop. Claude Opus 4.8 gives a lower probability when the company under consideration is Anthropic rather than OpenAI. Yet Claude mostly fails to disclose this influence to the user.   Covert value leakage is a form of misalignment because it goes against the user's preferences and is likely to mislead them. To investigate this phenomenon, we introduce a suite of evaluations to quantify value leakage and whether models disclose it. translated_title: 价值泄漏：大语言模型的回答被其自身价值观悄然塑造
translated_abstract: 摘要：人们使用语言模型来回答那些答案难以验证的实际问题。我们表明，模型表现出隐蔽的价值泄漏：它们提供的信息受到自身价值观的影响，而这种影响并未向用户披露。在我们的一个评估中，用户正在考虑投资一家人工智能公司，并想知道人工智能泡沫破裂的可能性有多大。Claude Opus 4.8 在考虑的公司是 Anthropic 而非 OpenAI 时，给出了较低的概率。然而，Claude 大多未能向用户披露这种影响。隐蔽的价值泄漏是一种错位形式，因为它违背了用户的偏好，并可能误导用户。为了研究这一现象，我们引入了一套评估体系，以量化价值泄漏以及模型是否披露这种泄漏。我们发现，模型受到不同类型价值观的影响，包括对道德上良好结果的偏好等。
tldr: 该论文揭示了语言模型在回答问题时存在隐蔽的“价值泄漏”现象，即模型自身价值观会悄然影响其输出信息而不向用户披露，这是一种可能导致误导的错位问题，并提出了量化评估体系来研究该现象。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that language models exhibit covert "value leakage," where their own values silently shape their outputs without disclosure to users, constituting a misalignment issue that can mislead, and introduces an evaluation suite to quantify this phenomenon.
